findings.item: Execution and liveness model (principle 2 vs brief's run-all/step-in)
findings.issue: The packet is internally inconsistent. It promises a 'cheap preview within about 100 ms' and also says 'mark downstream stale instead of silently recomputing'. Grasshopper users expect auto-solve on every change, while wind, energy and daylight modules take seconds to minutes. The packet never says which nodes run live and which wait for Run, so stale badges will appear on everything or nothing. NN/g's 0.1 s limit applies to the UI's acknowledgement, not to analysis results.
findings.fix: Add a 'cost class' to each module manifest. Live nodes (<100 ms) auto-run. Interactive nodes (<1 s) auto-run after a 300 ms debounce. Batch nodes run on demand and show a stale badge. Add a global 'Auto-run cheap nodes' toggle (the Grasshopper solver-lock precedent). The 100 ms target becomes 'slider echo and geometry proxy', not 'result'. Benchmark Observable's reactive notebooks and cite Tanimoto's liveness levels (LIVE 2013) for the model.

findings.issue: The rail 'Basic -> Advanced -> Present' mixes an expertise level (basic/advanced) with workflow stages. The brief's real journey is import/model massing -> tag program -> evaluate -> schematic design -> present. A beginner may be in Evaluate and an expert in Massing, so the rail cannot say where the user is. It also overlaps with the separate Essentials/Advanced drawer.
findings.fix: Make the rail the workflow stages (Massing, Program, Evaluate, Design, Present), each free to jump to and each with a completeness indicator. Make Essentials/Advanced a separate disclosure setting per module (or global). Document the mapping in PRODUCT.md. Test the two-axis model in the 3-task study.

findings.issue: Global undo across canvas, inspector and assumptions, palette commands, autosave, named snapshots, deterministic JSON and later graph diff and Yjs presence all depend on one state and command layer. The packet never chooses one. Retrofitting undo after 13 Nov is the classic rewrite trap.
findings.fix: Before coding, decide on a single command bus: every user action (palette, keyboard, drag, AI edit) is a serialisable command applied to one store. Two options: a Zustand store with zundo (temporal undo), or a Yjs document with Y.UndoManager (this also enables presence later). Spike for half a day and record the choice in CLAUDE.md. Keep React Flow as a view of the store, not the source of truth.

findings.issue: The packet lists the Cognitive Dimensions tutorial as an unreadable binary PDF, but its text extracts fine (Green and Blackwell, v1.2, 1998). Green and Petre (1996, JVLC 7(2):131-174) is the standard usability framework for dataflow languages, and it was not applied. Concretely, named Sender/Receiver relays create 'hidden dependencies', auto-reconnection is an 'error-proneness' issue, and frames and colours are 'secondary notation'.
findings.fix: Run a Cognitive Dimensions walkthrough of the node-canvas contract, at minimum covering viscosity, hidden dependencies, premature commitment, secondary notation, progressive evaluation and visibility. Add these rules: selecting a relay highlights all its partners and offers 'jump to'. Every module can run on partial inputs with placeholder warnings (progressive evaluation). Grouping, colour and notes never change semantics.

findings.issue: Flow is sourced from Wikipedia. Mark et al. (CHI 2008) is flagged unverified although an open PDF exists, and its finding is narrower than the packet implies. Notification timing has no empirical basis. Iqbal and Bailey (CHI 2008) showed that delivering notifications at task breakpoints lowered frustration and reaction time.
findings.fix: Cite Mark et al. correctly: interrupted email tasks were finished faster with equal quality, but with more stress, frustration, time pressure and effort, and interruption context made no difference. Add a rule to defer non-critical notifications and community activity to breakpoints (run finished, phase switch, save). Never interrupt during a drag, wire or text edit. Replace Wikipedia with Csikszentmihalyi's primary work, or drop the citation.

findings.issue: The goals are aesthetic and attentional, but the planned sessions record nothing comparable. The packet's line 'the aesthetic-usability effect can make a pretty UI look usable' has no source (Kurosu and Kashimura 1995).
findings.fix: For the five think-aloud sessions and the 3-task test, pre-define task success, time on task, errors and wrong turns, NASA-TLX (raw), UMUX-Lite or SUS, and a short flow scale (e.g. Rheinberg/Engeser Flow Short Scale). Repeat with the same tasks after 13 Nov to measure change. Cite the aesthetic-usability source or remove the claim.

findings.item: Competing status systems on node cards
findings.issue: One node can show 7 run states, a warning badge and 3 evidence statuses, which is about 10 semantic colours, beyond Carbon's caution of five or six. The 'Team assumption' ochre (#8A5A00, dark #E3B341) sits in the same hue family as a typical 'warning' amber. The packet never assigns run-state colours, so this collision is likely.
findings.fix: Set a hierarchy. Run state is an icon plus word in the node header, using neutral or cool colours, with red reserved for failed. Evidence status is not shown per value on the card. Instead show one aggregate chip (e.g. '2 assumptions, 1 FALSE'), with detail in the inspector and in 'Why this number?'. Give 'warning' a triangle shape and a hue clearly separate from team-assumption ochre, and document the full semantic palette in one table.

findings.item: React Flow defaults vs planned shortcuts
findings.issue: The packet says 'Delete removes edges', but the default deleteKeyCode is 'Backspace'. Space is both panActivationKeyCode and the select key for focused nodes. zoomOnDoubleClick conflicts with 'canvas double-click opens search'. Shift is box-select. Grasshopper users expect the Delete key.
findings.fix: Write an explicit shortcut map and set the props: deleteKeyCode=['Delete','Backspace'], zoomOnDoubleClick=false, and a non-Space pan key or pan-on-drag only. Skip shortcuts while focus is inside text inputs. Publish one cheat sheet and test it in the keyboard pass.

findings.issue: 'Wire flow animates only during a run' can last longer than 5 s next to other content, which triggers WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A). React Flow's animated edges are CSS animations, so MotionConfig reducedMotion='user' does not cover them.
findings.fix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion CSS rule that stops edge dash animation, provide a 'pause animations' control, and fall back to a static 'running' icon on the node. Add both to the a11y checklist.

findings.item: FALSE ASSUMPTION styling and colour-vision deficiency
findings.issue: Strikethrough lowers legibility of text that must stay readable, and most screen readers do not announce it. The three light-theme tokens have near-identical luminance (relative Y 0.108-0.127, computed), so they are indistinguishable in greyscale prints. A protanopia simulation (Machado 2009, CIELAB ΔE76) halves the blue-magenta difference, from about 66 to about 32.
findings.fix: Use the hatch, border, icon and the visible word 'FALSE ASSUMPTION' (also in the accessible name). Drop the strikethrough or apply it only to the superseded value, never to the explanation. Use different patterns for print and boards. Keep the computed contrast; the ≥5.4:1 claim holds (5.43-9.13).

findings.issue: OpenAI's guide (read 21 Oct) caps output at 3840 px per edge and 8,294,400 px, and calls output above 2560x1440 experimental. A full A2 sheet at 300 dpi is about 34.8 MP. The packet records the cap but no layout rule. The guide now names gpt-image-2.5 variants, so model IDs drift.
findings.fix: Present-mode rule: show an AI render's effective dpi on the board and warn below about 150 dpi. Disclose any upscaling in the caption ('AI-assisted, upscaled'). Store the exact model ID and size request in the prompt log. Size hero images to available pixels instead of stretching them.

findings.item: Viewport theme vs analysis colour maps
findings.issue: The packet themes the viewport separately but gives no rule linking background luminance to the ends of sequential maps. Light map ends vanish on white, and dark ends vanish on a dark viewport. Simultaneous contrast also shifts perceived values.
findings.fix: Use a mid-grey neutral viewport for analysis display in both themes, or ensure both ends of every shipped ramp reach 3:1 against the viewport background (check in CI with Culori). Draw the context and ground in neutral greys.

findings.issue: The packet relies on a Wikipedia article with an LLM-text warning. Sailer and Homner's meta-analysis (Educ Psychol Rev 2020, 32:77-112) finds small positive effects: g=.49 cognitive, .36 motivational, .25 behavioural. Game fiction and social interaction moderate the behavioural effects. The packet only lists bans and gives no positive, learning-supportive engagement design.
findings.fix: Cite Sailer and Homner. Label the ban on leaderboards and streaks as a values decision, not an evidence finding. Add positive mechanics: visible consequences after each run ('what changed' diff), progressive shortcut hints, evidence-completeness per stage, and attribution credit on forks.

findings.issue: The HAX 18 guidelines are marked unreadable (poster image), but Amershi et al., CHI 2019, list them in text. The AI principle therefore cites no specific guideline.
findings.fix: Map the AI rule to Amershi G1 and G2 (what the system can do, how well), G9 (support efficient correction), G11 (explain why), G15 (encourage feedback) and G18 (notify about changes), using the CHI 2019 paper.

findings.issue: The benchmarks are mostly text claims. There are no screenshots or annotated captures. Forma comes from a mirror, the Spline editor and Rerun UI were not viewed, and Observable's dataflow UX was not studied.
findings.fix: Add one annotated screenshot per benchmark (Figma, Linear, Speckle and Forma first), with 'copy' and 'avoid' callouts. Add Observable as a liveness and stale-state benchmark.

false_assumptions.claim: Mark et al. CHI 2008 cannot be read; interruption raises stress and cost (UNVERIFIED).
false_assumptions.why_false: An open PDF is available. The paper found that interrupted tasks were completed faster with no difference in quality, at the price of more stress, frustration, time pressure and effort. Interruption context made no difference.
false_assumptions.correction: Cite it as 'faster but more stressed', not as a time cost. Use it to justify protecting edit sessions from interruptions.

false_assumptions.claim: The Cognitive Dimensions tutorial is a binary PDF that could not be read.
false_assumptions.why_false: The PDF's text extracts normally: Green and Blackwell, 'Cognitive Dimensions of Information Artefacts: a tutorial', v1.2, October 1998, 75 pages.
false_assumptions.correction: Apply the CD framework (Green and Petre 1996, JVLC 7(2)) to the node-canvas contract.

false_assumptions.why_false: The React Flow API reference gives deleteKeyCode the default 'Backspace'. The accessibility page does not document deletion as a feature.
false_assumptions.correction: Set deleteKeyCode to ['Delete','Backspace'] explicitly. Also set zoomOnDoubleClick=false so double-click can open search.

false_assumptions.claim: Microsoft HAX Toolkit's 18 guidelines are unreadable (poster image).
false_assumptions.why_false: The guidelines are published as text in Amershi et al., CHI 2019, and on Microsoft Research pages. They comprise 18 guidelines in four phases, starting with 'Make clear what the system can do'.
false_assumptions.correction: Cite the CHI 2019 paper and map specific guidelines to the AI-assistance rules.

false_assumptions.claim: Gamification evidence for learning is 'mixed' (from Wikipedia).
false_assumptions.why_false: A peer-reviewed meta-analysis reports small but significant positive effects: g=.49 cognitive (stable in rigorous studies), .36 motivational and .25 behavioural (less stable).
false_assumptions.correction: Cite Sailer and Homner (2020). Frame the no-leaderboard policy as an ethical choice and allow learning-supportive feedback mechanics.

verdict: Round 2 fixed most of round 1. The Base UI default, the React Flow UI Pro status, the keyboard wiring plan and the factual corrections all check out against sources, and the status-token contrast holds (5.43:1 or higher). What remains is design logic, not facts. The packet has no liveness model, so the 100 ms preview, stale propagation and Grasshopper's auto-solve habit conflict. The phase rail mixes expertise level with workflow stage. No state/command layer underpins undo and snapshots. Run states and evidence statuses compete on one node card. The visual-programming and attention research is thin: it skips Cognitive Dimensions and mis-cites or calls unreadable papers that are openly available. Fix these before coding the 13 Nov core.
